guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: nasal wah-fuzz riff into dirty British amp; raw 60s/70s psychedelic hard rock texture
tone.profile: nasal wah-fuzz riff into dirty British amp; raw 60s/70s psychedelic hard rock texture
tone.summary: Gate -> Boost -> Wah -> Fuzz -> UK 45 Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab. This chain emphasizes upper-mids, grit, and raw British crunch.
corrections: make fuzz more nasal and gated
delay should be minimal or none

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - Whole Lotta Love - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise inherent in high-gain fuzz/wah usage.
Slightly push the signal into the fuzz/wah circuit and enhance upper-mids for bite.
blocks.gap: No specific boost needed, but a slight gain lift helps drive the subsequent pedals.

blocks.purpose: Provide the signature nasal wah sweep required for the riffing.
Generate the aggressive, nasal, and gated fuzz tone characteristic of the era.
Simulate the raw, upper-mid heavy British Plexi/Marshall sound.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid punch.
Fine-tune the frequency response, emphasizing the upper mids for maximum bite and cutting through the mix.
Optional subtle modulation for texture, but kept off to avoid 'lush delay' feel.
blocks.gap: The target avoids lush effects; Chorus is used minimally if needed, otherwise this slot could be left empty or filled with a simple Volume control.

blocks.purpose: Disabled to ensure minimal or no delay, per the 'corrections' list.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the raw, aggressive upper-mids required for 60s/70s hard rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance raw upper-mid punch and grit for the era's sound.
